sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of High-Voltage Power Transformers and Switchgear

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1984, as amended by the 2007 Additional Protocol for Road Victim Protection and Investment Protection)
France–China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income, signed 30 May 1984, as amended by the 2013 Protocol
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union – Freedom of Establishment (Article 49) and Free Movement of Capital (Article 63)
OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI, 2016) – France–residents covered tax treaty interplay

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) Articles L.561-2-1, L.561-2-2, L.561-45 to L.561-57; French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles L.123-1, L.123-33, R.123-53 and R.123-223; Decree No. 2016-724 of 1 June 2016 on UBO declarations; implementation of Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD 4), Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD 5), and FATF Recommendations (2012, revised 2023).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Extract of the Corporate Registry / Certificate of Incorporation and Current Officers of each Foreign Corporate Shareholder (e.g., ultimate holding company) demonstrating the chain of control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or commercial court registrar in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention (if the issuing jurisdiction is a Contracting State); otherwise full Consular Legalization through the French Embassy or Consulate with appropriate chain of certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Pouvoir) granted by the shareholders to the incorporators and to the future President of the SAS, including authority to sign the Articles of Association (Statuts) and to open the corporate bank account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of residence or in France (Notaire de Paris)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille (if foreign); if the document must be presented to the French bank or to the Registry, additionally a certified French translation by a sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) registered with a Cour d'appel

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Passport / National Identity Document of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) holding 25% or more of the SAS capital or control rights, and of the President (Président) of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National authority of the UBO's or President's country of citizenship (e.g., Ministry of Interior, Consulate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy and Hague Apostille (if foreign national), accompanied by a sworn French translation; for domestic French nationals, only a simple certified copy is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Domiciliation Certificate (Attestation de domiciliation) or Lease Contract (Bail) evidencing the availability of the SAS registered office in France for at least the first 12 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered domiciliation company (société de domiciliation agréée) or the landlord/co-owner of the premises
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: French domestic act: no apostille required, but must be certified by the domiciliation company or notarized if a private lease; if the lessor is a foreign entity, the lease shall be notarized, apostilled and translated into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Articles of Association (Projet de Statuts) of the SAS, including UBO identification schedule and the French law-governed corporate governance rules (Président, Décisions collectives, Commissaire aux comptes appointment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French Avocat (counsel) or Notaire for the founders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cash-founded SAS Statuts may be executed sous seing privé (private signature) without notarization; mandatory notarization only if real-property or specific assets are contributed in kind (apport en nature)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against: (i) the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EU Council Implementing Regulations under CFSP), (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the French Ministry of Economy and Finance (Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Relance) sanctions and assets-freezing list, (iv) ORCOM and TRACFIN typologies for high-risk jurisdictions, (v) OFAC SDN List as a secondary bank-onboarding filter for any USD clearing, and (vi) FATF high-risk jurisdiction call lists. PEP status is determined under Article R.561-18 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, requiring enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, plus senior management approval for any high-risk PEP relationship. For a Low_Risk_Standard heavy electrical equipment manufacturer (ISIC 2710) with no statutory license, simplified/normal due diligence is retained, but any shareholder from a non-transparent or high-risk jurisdiction will escalate the customer risk rating to 'enhanced'.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by the French State at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; name availability and prior-rights screening against the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via INPI's data.inpi.fr and legacy Infogreffe Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) checks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All registration filings and the Articles of Association must be drafted in French (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994, Loi Toubon, and Article L.121-1 of the French Commercial Code). The company name must be writable in Latin script; any non-Latin characters in trade names must be transliterated and the Latin version will be registered in the RNE. The legal form suffix 'SAS' must appear immediately after the corporate name. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to names already registered in the RNE for the same or similar activity, nor to protected trademarks registered with INPI.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank – requires prior authorization from the ACPR (Prudential Control and Resolution Authority)
Assurance (insurance), Mutuelle, Mutuelle d'Assurance – reserved for licensed insurance entities
Crédit (credit, finance) – restricted and subject to ACPR or Banque de France authorization
Courtier, Agent d'Affaires – regulated brokerage terms
Notaire, Avocat, Huissier de Justice, Expert-Comptable – reserved for regulated professions
Ambassade, Consulat, Préfecture, Ministère, Président de la République, République, Service Public, État – misleading official/sovereign association (prohibited)
Chambre de Commerce, Chambre des Métiers – reserved to public chambers
SAFER, CGI, and any token suggesting state monopoly or public mandate
CE, Communauté Européenne, Union Européenne, France (in a national-emblem context) – requires caution and cannot mislead as to state sponsorship
SA, SARL, EURL, SNC (alternative legal suffix) – inconsistent with the SAS form and prohibited in the corporate name
Solid-State Transformer, Transfo – not prohibited but will be screened against ISIC 2710 class protection
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not issue a standalone name-reservation certificate prior to incorporation; protection is achieved either (i) by filing the full M0 incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique, which is examined by the INPI (Registre National des Entreprises) and the competent commercial court registry, or (ii) by depositing a French trademark with INPI. Upon rejection, the INPI notifies a formal 'Avis d'Observation / Rejet' within 5 working days. The applicant then has 15 days (extendable to 30 days upon reasoned request) to rectify the Statuts and resubmit through the Guichet Unique. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may: (a) file an administrative protest (recours hiérarchique) to the INPI Director General, (b) request the President of the competent Tribunal judiciaire or Tribunal de commerce to order the registry to proceed, using the full commercial court summary procedure (référé), or (c) select a new name variant and re-file without prejudice to any third-party trademark action. In parallel, the applicant should register the intended name as a French trademark (INPI, class 9/35/37/42) to secure priority for a 10-year term. The 30-day validity window in this protocol corresponds to the maximum statutory response period for a registry deficiency notice and the standard opposition horizon; after that period the filing must be refreshed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with restrictions: French law (Article L.123-11-1 of the Commercial Code and Decree No. 84-406, as amended) allows the SAS to be domiciled via a licensed commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) for the duration of the lease, including 'virtual' arrangements for the legal seat, provided the registered office does not constitute a shell. However, for ISIC 2710 heavy electrical equipment manufacturing (solid-state transformers, high-voltage switchgear), the commercial reality of a purely virtual office is not sustainable: a manufacturer must establish an operational establishment (établissement principal) in France for ISO/CE conformity, customs valuation, VAT invoicing, and industrial liability. INPI and tax authorities may strike the company if the registered office is shown to be purely fictitious. Virtual domiciliation is acceptable during pre-operational incorporation (3-6 months) but must be replaced by a physical industrial site for production, warehousing, and technical staff; recommended to secure both the legal seat and operational establishment within the same French region.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-high overall (approx. 35-45% within the first 24 months). Unannounced physical inspections are statistically likely in the following categories: (i) INSEE/RNE substance checks where domiciliation is registered at a commercial address with many companies; (ii) tax audits by DGFiP focused on transfer pricing and CFC substance for non-resident-owned SAS; (iii) environmental (IED/ICPE) inspections for transformer manufacturing (oil/insulation gases, heavy metal) by DREAL; (iv) social security URSSAF on-site visits for employee presence; and (v) pre-opening inspections by the Customs and VAT departments if the company imports components from outside the EU. For a pure virtual office without any operational establishment, the probability of a physical inspection escalates to approximately 70% in the first 12 months, with potential reclassification of the registered office and nullification risk under Article 1831 of the Civil Code and Article L.210-2 of the Commercial Code.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation UBO piercing and AML/CFT due-diligence legal opinion (identification of all shareholders ≥25%, verification of non-resident ownership chain, sanctions/PEP screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French Avocat / law firm (commercial and banking regulatory desk)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: EUR 2,500-4,500 for a straightforward cross-border SAS incorporation; fixed-fee quote including screening database reports

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance screening against RNE/INPI and drafting of the French Articles of Association (Statuts SAS) with SAS governance and ISIC 2710 object clause
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French Avocat / legal counsel (with notarial backup)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for mid-complexity SAS drafting: EUR 1,200-2,500 exclusive of official fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translations (traductions assermentées) of foreign corporate documents, certificates, passports, powers of attorney and UBO documentary evidence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) registered with a French Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory/reputable per-word tariff; approximately EUR 0.10-0.25 per word for complex corporate documentation, plus certification fee per bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille / consular legalization of foreign documents (Covid-modified signature chains, French consular fees in the shareholder's country)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary of origin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state (Hague apostille authority), French Consulate if required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Tarif notarial in the issuing jurisdiction + French consular fee schedule (approx. EUR 50-150 per document) + courier/handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation contract with a licensed domiciliation company (3-month pre-operational period, if a physical industrial site is not yet leased)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Société de domiciliation agréée (licensed under Article L.123-11-1 of the Commercial Code)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 150-450 per year; pro-rata 3-month startup charge plus setup fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice (Avis de Constitution) in a legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales - JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: JAL approved by the Prefecture, as selected by the founders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per line fixed by the Prefecture; for SAS incorporations typical range EUR 150-300 (approx. 12-20 lines)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official incorporation and registration filing fee (M0 dossier) covering the Guichet Unique, INPI/RNE registry, and issuance of the Kbis extract by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (paid through Guichet Unique)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory official tariff schedule for SAS creation (approx. EUR 384-430 as published for 2025, inclusive of registry tax and lump-sum taxe sur les associations non profit No)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration (Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No separate statutory fee; included in the comprehensive SAS registration tariff; penalty risk (EUR 7,500 fine per Article L.561-49 of the Monetary and Financial Code) avoided by accurate filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening support documentation (certified copies, apostilled directors' documents, bank's AML/KYC external screening, and legal validation of the bank dossier)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French bank (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole) compliance department and counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Preparatory counsel services and administrative certification cost; banks charge EUR 0-250 under the agreements; external estimate for expedited dossier preparation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Digital PEP and sanctions screening platform subscription (initial screening + 90-day monitoring of all UBOs/directors)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party screening provider (e.g., Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, World-Check/Refinitiv, or a French LRQA-like provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription fee for a company of small size, bundled entity and UBO coverage for one year; recurring cost thereafter

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI trademark research and optional priority filing of the company name in international classes 9, 35, 37, and 42 (defensive name protection)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official INPI tariff: EUR 190 electronic application for one class plus additional class fees (EUR 40 per additional class up to 3); plus attorney preparation fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for additional apostille/legalization, document corrections, and notarial minutes (reserve bracket)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaries, apostille authorities, and administrative agencies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Reasonable reserve of approx. 8-10% of pre-incorporation cost base to absorb venue-specific tariff differences (statutory fee guidelines)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (SAS regime), L.210-2, L.210-7, and R.123-37 et seq. (registration formalities); French Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement), Articles L.181-1 et seq. and L.511-1, for the subsequent ICPE licensing phase.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS - Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) in the department of the SAS registered office, receiving the filing electronically through the national Guichet Unique operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts dûment signés (signed articles of association), accompanied by the certificat de dépôt des fonds (capital deposit certificate), attestation de parution of the legal announcement, and déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs, submitted as the Dossier unique de création d'entreprise on the INPI Guichet Unique (successor to the former Cerfa/Imprimé M0).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by French law for an SAS; the capital is fixed freely in the articles (e.g., EUR 1,000). Cash contributions must be deposited by the subscribers in a blocked trust account with a bank, notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and remain escrowed until the RCS registration extract (Kbis) is obtained, after which the funds are released to the Président on behalf of the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: the founders accept full subscription and cash payment of the Company's share capital of EUR 1,000 represented by 1,000 ordinary shares of EUR 1.00 each, per the capital subscription certificate. RESOLVED FURTHER: the registered office is fixed at 25 Rue de la Paix, 75002 Paris, France, under the jurisdiction of the Paris Commercial Registry. RESOLVED FURTHER: [Name] is appointed Président with full power to bind the Company, and [Name] is appointed statutory auditor as required; each appointee accepts. RESOLVED FURTHER: these resolutions take effect upon registration and counsel is authorized to file the formation dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution, notary public, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a dedicated non-withdrawable account in the proposed corporate name; collect KYC documentation from all shareholders; receive the cash subscriptions in full; obtain the funded capital deposit certificate from the depositary. Keep the funds blocked until the Kbis extract is tendered by the legal representative after registration.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (statuts)
Passport or national ID of each shareholder
Proof of taxpayer identification for beneficial owners
Evidence of source of funds for each cash contribution
Power of attorney if any founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues an AML/KYC query under the Code monétaire et financier (Article L.561-5), deliver the supplemental documentation promptly; if the bank refuses the deposit, transfer the funds to a notary or to the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations without altering the statutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Statutes and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All founders (shareholders); optional notary in the registered-office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the statutes covering corporate name, purpose (manufacture of power transformers and switchgear), duration (max. 99 years), share classes and rights, governance structure, appointment of the Président, statutory auditor thresholds, and the registered-office lease; have each founder or their proxy initial every page and sign the final page, with notarization if real property is contributed.
required_dossiers: Final statutory draft incorporating the first board resolution
Registered-office lease or domiciliation agreement
Powers of attorney for signatories
Identity documents of officers and shareholders
Capital deposit certificate issued at Step 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a formal defect is identified before filing, execute a corrective deed (acte rectificatif) signed by the same parties; any substantial amendment to capital or officers must be re-approved by the shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal-announcement newspaper (Journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Insert the mandatory notice stating the corporate form (SAS), corporate name, registered office, share capital, purpose, duration, appointees, and the commercial registry where the filing will be made; request the attestation de parution certifying the publication; preserve the issue and invoice for the filing dossier.
required_dossiers: Signed statutes (full text for reference)
Draft notice conforming to Article R.123-105 of the Commercial Code
Payment of the publication fee
Declaration of corporate officers for inclusion in the notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected or contains errors, publish a corrective notice and obtain a new attestation; only approved legal-announcement journals (JALs habilités) are acceptable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission at the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), transmitting automatically to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online creation questionnaire for an SAS; upload the signed statutes, capital deposit certificate, publication attestation, registered-office proof, identity documents of the Président and beneficial owners; execute the definitive share subscription and the declaration of non-disqualification; pay the registry fee and track the dossier for any supplemental requests.
required_dossiers: Signed and paginated statutes
Capital deposit certificate from the depositary
Attestation de parution (legal announcement attestation)
Registered-office address evidence (lease or bail)
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (beneficial-owner form)
Identity and address proof of the Président and any delegated managers
Declarations of no disqualification for the officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Reply to any supplemental request within the portal-prescribed period (ordinarily 15 calendar days); on refusal of registration, resubmit the corrected dossier or seize the competent registrar and, if necessary, the presiding judge of the Tribunal de Commerce through a written claim, with amendment of defective documents before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Kbis, Tax and Social Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE (SIRENE); DGFiP; URSSAF; DGDDI for customs identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the original Kbis extract evidencing RCS entry and the allocated SIREN/SIRET numbers; await automatic communication to the business register and enrollment for VAT at DGFiP; open and validate the employer account at URSSAF and obtain the French EORI number from DGDDI if components such as laminated cores or copper windings will be imported for transformer assembly.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract (first original issue)
SIREN/SIRET notification from INSEE
National VAT identification confirmation from DGFiP
EORI customs identifier application for cross-border component imports (DGDDI)
Officer identity documents for social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT or SIRET notification does not arrive within the regulatory window, apply to the local SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) for a certificate of identification and request official reactivation; any mismatch in company data is corrected through a rectification filing at the Guichet Unique.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) acting under the Ministry of Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion, together with the Préfet du département for ICPE authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation environnementale / Arrêté préfectoral d'enregistrement (or récépissé de déclaration where applicable) issued under the ICPE regime (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement), Articles L.181-1 et seq. and L.511-1 of the French Environmental Code, authorizing the manufacture, assembly and testing of power and solid-state transformers.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL - Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (environmental protection division of the Prefecture)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: ICPE Enregistrement for a medium-capacity transformer manufacturing and coating plant, or Déclaration with a simplified environmental study if the activity and auxiliary oil-storage volumes are below the authorization thresholds; a full EIA (étude d'impact) and public inquiry are required when the installation falls within Annex R.122-2 of the Environmental Code, notably where oil storage exceeds heavy-oil thresholds or coating/VOC capacity is significant.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Applicable ICPE ministerial standard orders (arrêtés-types): wastewater pH 6.0-8.5, suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L, hydrocarbons ≤ 5 mg/L, COD ≤ 300 mg/L; VOC emission limits and a solvent management plan under Directive 2004/42/EC; dielectric fluids and waste transformer oils tested PCB-free per EU Regulation 2019/1021; hazardous waste (varnish, resin, oils) transported and treated only by licensed ADR-compliant facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for industrial premises from the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) and the local safety commission; structural load verification and electrical conformity certificate (Consuel) from an approved technical inspection body; workplace clearance opened with the DREETS (labor inspectorate) and CARSAT covering high-voltage and machinery safety, ergonomics, ventilation and fire-exit compliance before commercial production begins.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — official portal: impots.gouv.fr (professional area: Portail Fiscal des Professionnels). Company formalities run through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. VAT identification is issued by the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); customs export formalities are administered by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) at pro.douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS and for foreign entities establishing a French operation: (1) file the incorporation or branch-registration file with the Guichet Unique to obtain the SIREN/SIRET; (2) lodge the statutory business commencement (début d'activité) declaration with the SIE; (3) the DGFiP then issues the definitive intra-community VAT number (FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN), normally within 8-10 working days; (4) non-EU-established persons liable for VAT in France must additionally appoint a jointly and severally liable fiscal representative under Art. 289 A CGI; EU suppliers may cover distance sales through the OSS/IOSS without a French fixed establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box regime. Statutory elections relevant to a SAS: (i) option for French fiscal integration (intégration fiscale, Art. 223 A CGI) for a 95%-owned French group; (ii) election, for newly created SMEs, to be taxed as a pass-through on French income tax for up to five fiscal years (Art. 239 bis AB CGI); (iii) no elective hybrid-mismatch designations — ATAD2 anti-hybrid provisions (Arts. 209, 212 bis, 212 ter CGI) apply compulsorily. The SAS therefore defaults to full entity-level corporate income tax (IS).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French value added tax; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC implemented in Code Général des Impôts, Arts. 256-289 C)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise en base de TVA: EUR 85,000 annual turnover for goods supplies (the rule governing an ISIC 2710 manufacturer) and EUR 37,500 for services; the higher tolerance (seuil majoré) is EUR 93,500 for goods and EUR 41,000 for services. Foreign distance sellers established outside the EU are taxable on their first euro of French B2C sales; EU-established sellers use the EUR 10,000 intra-EU OSS threshold. French registration becomes compulsory once turnover exceeds EUR 85,000 of goods in the preceding calendar year (rolling test).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France implements the EU e-invoicing reform (facturation électronique) through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) interconnected with certified partner dematerialization platforms (PDPs). There is no Italian-style fiscal-stamping clearance: the PPF validates the mandatory 45-field DGFiP data schema and the transmission pipeline. B2B domestic invoices must be issued as structured e-invoices (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) and exchanged through a PDP; cross-border B2B, export, and B2C supplies are covered by mandatory e-reporting in near real time. The phased timeline starts 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and mid-caps, and 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-entities.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Outbound exports of goods from French customs territory to destinations outside the EU are definitively exempt with full right to input VAT deduction (exportation exonérée, Art. 262-I-1 CGI); intra-EU dispatches to a buyer identified for VAT in another Member State are exempt under Art. 262 ter-1 CGI. Ancillary services (transport, loading, expert supervision) follow the export exemption. Offshore B2B services (e.g., engineering or embedded software supporting solid-state transformers) are zero-rated where the customer is a taxable person established outside the EU (place-of-supply rule, Art. 259 A CGI). Eligibility requires physical exit of the goods within the statutory 90-day (3-month) window and full evidentiary support of the transport movement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (connaissement) or equivalent transport document (CMR road consignment note, air waybill)
Inward Remittance Certificate (attestation de change) from the authorized bank evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
For intra-EU dispatches: buyer's EU VAT ID and the EC Sales List / Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens (DES)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP audits export zero-rating strictly. Missing or falsified export evidence triggers re-levy of VAT on the seller (Art. 272 CGI), a 40% negligence penalty or 80% bad-faith/fraud penalty (Art. 1729 CGI), and late-payment interest of 0.20% per month (Art. 1727 CGI); the non-EU fiscal representative is jointly liable. Tax-fraud conviction under Art. 1741 CGI carries up to EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years' imprisonment. The VAT recovery period is 3 years (LPF Art. L. 169), extended to 6 years for concealed activity and up to 10 years for cross-border fraud; customs penalties (Code des douanes Arts. 414-423) may add up to twice the evaded duties with seizure of goods and retrospective clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Paris) exercises monetary authority and balance-of-payments statistics; banking prudential licensing and AML supervision are delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR); foreign-exchange control regulations are codified in Articles L151-1 to L153-8 of the French Code monétaire et financier (CMF), administered jointly by Banque de France and the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) for investment screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). France imposes no exchange-control authorization, no conversion quota, and no profit-repatriation license. Capital account entries are free except for (i) inbound foreign direct investment in restricted sectors requiring prior authorization under CMF Article L151-3 and Decree No. 2019-1590 — power transformer manufacturing (ISIC 2710) is not a listed sensitive sector, although a preliminary DG Trésor screening questionnaire is prudent when the ultimate parent is non-EU; and (ii) balance-of-payments statistical reporting to Banque de France for every cross-border flow of EUR 750,000 or more per transaction (aggregated by calendar month). Profit remittance: dividends paid by a French SAS to a non-resident corporate shareholder are subject to 25% domestic withholding tax, reduced to 0% for EU/EEA corporate shareholders meeting the 2-year holding condition under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU), and reduced to 0%-15% under applicable double-tax treaties (e.g., 15% under the France-China treaty at a 10% threshold; 0% under France-US treaty at an 80% ownership and 2-year holding threshold). There are no exchange-control hurdles to dividend transfer; only standard tax filings (Form 2561-B, or the crediting institution withholds and files 2777-SD for the 25% rate) are required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio; exporters may freely hold export receipts in euro or in foreign-currency accounts. No forced repatriation deadline exists beyond commercial credit terms. Compliance obligations are purely statistical: export receipts of EUR 750,000 or more (per transaction or cumulative monthly) must be reported to Banque de France through the authorized intermediary bank, with the exporter supplying the transaction motive code (nomenclature des motifs monétaires et financiers), contract reference, and underlying invoice. Exports of ISIC 2710/HS 8504 products are zero-rated for VAT (exigibilité after delivery); the exporter must retain proof of export (bill of lading, customs exit validation in the DELTA customs system) to sustain the zero-rating upon audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR/USD multi-currency account with SWIFT corporate access and embedded documentary credit windows; dedicated capital escrow sub-account for shareholder-funded capex
Operational treasury account plus trade-finance envelope (LC issuing/confirming, MT700/MT760 guarantees) and FX forward drawing line
Treasury and trade solutions account for large-ticket documentary collections; medium-term project financing for factory build-out
Operational and liquidity account with commodity/trade-finance desk for transformer component imports and supply-chain finance
Regional SME operating account used as second clearing rail for SEPA supplier payments and payroll

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as a secondary liquidity and disbursement account; Low as the primary trade-finance or escrow institution. Qonto, Wise Business, and Shine are authorized by ACPR as payment institutions or electronic-money institutions under PSD2, offer French IBANs, and permit fully remote onboarding within 48-72 hours; they clear SEPA CT and can execute SWIFT MT103 wires through partner banks (e.g., BNP, Société Générale) at capped volumes. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot grant credit, cannot open or confirm documentary letters of credit in-house (LCs must be routed via the EMI's licensed banking partner), may reject funds from regulated industries without a banking license, and are subject to stricter transaction-velocity limits that are unsuitable for large-ticket transformer payments (typically EUR 100k-500k per wire). Recommendation: maintain an EMI account for administrative/disbursement agility while anchoring liquidity and documentary credits at a Tier-1 bank that provides a full SWIFT and LC platform.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not a statutory mandate: under CMF Article L561-5-1 and Article 4 of the Arrete of 30 July 2015, remote client identification is permissible via (a) an eIDAS-notified electronic identification scheme, or (b) a video-identification (visio-identification) procedure declared to the ACPR. In practice, Tier-1 French banks will require for a foreign-parent SAS: (i) a video KYC interview of all directors/shareholders with >25% economic benefit in French or English, (ii) notarized corporate documents with apostille (KBIS extract, statuts, RBE UBO filing), (iii) certified passport copies, and (iv) bank reference letters from the parent's home institution. Remote onboarding is achievable in 2-4 weeks; a physical visit to the Paris branch typically shortens clearance to 1-2 weeks and substantially reduces refusal risk for non-EU parents. Banque de France does not require local director presence for banking account opening; however, the SAS must demonstrate French substance (registered office, local management, or employees) to satisfy bank domiciliation checks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: bank cannot map the natural persons ultimately owning or controlling the SAS through a non-EU corporate parent chain, triggering CMF Article L561-5 enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unofficial and official UBO filing from the Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE); annotated group organigram showing every natural person with direct or indirect ownership >= 25%; notarized passport copies of all UBOs; certificate of incorporation and current register extract of the parent; board resolution of the parent approving the French entity's shareholding chain

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth deficiency: a high-value capital injection (e.g., > EUR 500,000 for factory setup) without a traceable trail, raising suspicion of undisclosed loans or circular funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the ultimate parent (last 2 years); 12-month bank statements of the investing shareholder showing accumulated operating profits; subscription agreement and call notices for the capital increase; statement by the Commissaire aux Comptes or a licensed accountant validating the source of funds; asset/liability breakdown of capital expenditure budget with supplier quotes

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow mismatch: declared scope (import of transformer components from Asia, export of finished HV equipment) without documentary support, creating red flags on goods not yet physically flowing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreement with the Asian OEM for solid-state transformer sub-assemblies; pro-forma invoices and air/sea freight quotations; Incoterms schedule and draft bills of lading; EORI registration evidence and customs broker mandate; preliminary export contracts with EU utilities and end-user certificates; HS 8504 customs classification memo

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening hit: counterparties or shareholders appearing on EU consolidated sanctions lists, particularly involving jurisdictions subject to export-control scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative PEP and sanctions screening report on all shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories (generated within 48 hours); valid end-user certificate for exported transformers; EU Dual-Use assessment or no-embargo attestation for ISIC 2710 power equipment; bank reference letter from the shareholder's home-country institution confirming legitimate commercial history

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Letterbox-company profile: SAS exhibiting no French substance (no premises, no local payroll, no operational expenditure) during the first-year onboarding review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bail or serviced-office agreement for the registered address; appointment letters of French director and local administrative officer; payroll records and social-charge payments (URSSAF) for the first employee; French utility and telecommunication invoices under the SAS name; dated photographs or lease certification of the operational premises

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execute via SWIFT MT103 from the parent's bank to the SAS's EUR account at a Tier-1 French bank, with Field 70 clearly declaring 'Apport en capital / capital increase' and the Banque de France motive code for capital contribution or shareholder loan (prêt d'actionnaire); Field 50 must show the exact ordering shareholder legal name; Field 57 must show the French bank BIC and the SAS IBAN; Field 72 must reference the board resolution date and the notarial or statutory deed reference. Compliance sequence: (i) prior shareholder resolution increasing the SAS capital; (ii) deposit of funds with the receiving bank evidenced by an attestation de dépôt des fonds; (iii) KBIS update recording the new share capital (within 1 month); (iv) the receiving bank files the Banque de France BOP return for flows >= EUR 750,000; (v) if the parent is non-EU, retain evidence that the DG Trésor screening (if applicable) was concluded. Do not split flows to stay under the EUR 750,000 reporting threshold; Banque de France aggregates by month. For capital escrow, the account must be blocked until the KBIS capital update is completed and releasing instructions signed by two authorized signatories per the bank mandate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred clearing rails in order: (1) Documentary Letter of Credit — issued via BNP Paribas or Societe Generale using SWIFT MT700 (issue), MT707 (amendment), MT720 (transfer) under UCP 600, availed by the beneficiary's confirming bank in EUR or USD; presenting documents include commercial invoice, packing list, full-set bill of lading or airway bill, certificate of quality, and (for Chinese suppliers) a certificate of origin or CCC certificate. (2) SWIFT MT103 for open-account settlements post-inspection — Field 70 must state 'Achat de composants transformateurs + contract reference', Field 72 the HS 8504 code, and the bank maps the flow to French customs/import statistics. (3) SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) for EU suppliers below EUR 100,000, cleared via Banque de France's Target2 participation. (4) Bank guarantees — advance-payment bonds and performance bonds via SWIFT MT760 to secure export contracts with EU utilities. All outbound flows must be reconciled against the underlying purchase orders; the bank may block payments if the economic substance (invoice, packing list, proof of transportation) is not uploaded to the corporate banking portal within the clearing window.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forwards (tenor 1-24 months) under an ISDA or FBF Master Agreement, collateralized at 0-10% CSA threshold depending on credit rating of the parent guarantor; no French regulatory restriction on forward cover for trade exposures
EUR/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for RMB-denominated component purchases, settled in EUR against the offshore CNH fixing, permissible when onshore CNY deliverability is restricted

EUR/USD and EUR/CNH cross-currency swaps for medium-term alignment of USD export receivables with EUR shareholder-loan liabilities; reported under EMIR to a registered trade repository, no mandatory central clearing for FX swaps

Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars (EUR call / USD put) to hedge large single-ticket export tenders; executed OTC with authorized counterparties, premium paid within standard account credit lines, subject to EMIR transaction reporting
Short-term FX swaps (swap de change) for rolling USD receipts into EUR funding for payroll and local suppliers without residual FX risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) via the Registre National des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in a court injunction, daily coercive penalties, and a civil fine generally of approximately EUR 1,500, increasing to approximately EUR 3,000 for repeated non-compliance. There is no automatic annual strike-off solely for late accounts; registry removal may follow prolonged inactivity, commonly after approximately three years and notice procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and required schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally electronically filed within three months after financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, interest for late payment, and additional penalties for inaccurate or incomplete declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information confirmation and update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the French beneficial ownership register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: France does not generally require a separate annual beneficial ownership confirmation. The SAS must verify the information annually as an internal control and file changes or newly reportable information within 30 days of the relevant event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate beneficial ownership information may result in court injunctions, fines for the company and responsible individuals, and restrictions or other measures affecting the company's registration status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder approval and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; no separate filing authority unless required information is included with the accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must generally approve the annual accounts and decide on profit allocation within six months after financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or document the annual decision may expose directors or officers to liability, permit court-ordered compliance, and impair the validity or evidentiary value of corporate decisions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of the following three thresholds: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million annual net turnover, or an average of 50 employees. Mandatory appointment may also apply in specified control or group situations and where statutory conditions otherwise require an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (Autorité des normes comptables). IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts or where legally permitted, but standalone statutory accounts are generally prepared under French GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO confirmation filing is generally required. The company must conduct an annual internal verification of ownership and control information and file any change within 30 days. Share transfers must be recorded in the share-transfer register and reflected in the register of shareholders and, where applicable, in the beneficial ownership filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders or Share Accounts
Register of Corporate Decisions and Minutes
Register of Directors or Officers, where maintained for governance and evidentiary purposes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-1,950 per year, depending on address, mail handling, domiciliation, and corporate secretarial services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 5,000-20,000 per year for a mandatory statutory audit of a privately held SAS, depending on turnover, group structure, transaction volume, inventory, and consolidation requirements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.0% (French standard corporate income tax / impôt sur les sociétés); an additional 3.3% social contribution applies to corporate income tax exceeding EUR 763,000, producing a maximum headline burden of approximately 25.825% for larger companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises with turnover below EUR 10 million benefit from a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit. Research and development expenditures may generate the Crédit d'Impôt Recherche and the Crédit d'Impôt Innovation, reducing the effective tax cost for autonomous transformer engineering activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa No. 2065 (2065-SD and accompanying schedule series 2050 through 2059, the French corporate laisse fiscale), filed by electronic mandatory platform EFI/ELM at impots.gouv.fr/professionnel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers, return must be filed by the second working day after 1 May (typically 2 to 5 May). For non-calendar fiscal years, filing is required within 95 days after the fiscal-year close. Quarterly instalments fall due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the balance payable at the time of annual filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, SIREN/SIRET, legal form, registered office, principal activity, tax office reference, fiscal year opening and closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French permanent establishment must indicate its own SIRET in France and the full registered address of the foreign corporate head office. The PE must use its French establishment identifier for all correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A / Comptabilité (fiscal result before adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss from the annual statutory accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the profit or loss attributable to the French permanent establishment under the separate-enterprise principle may be entered. Home-office general costs are not deductible unless allocated in accordance with Article 209 CGI and OECD principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B / Réintégrations et déductions (tax adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses, fines, penalties, excess depreciation, excessive interest, tax depreciation adjustments and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back expenses not economically related to the PE, or amounts benefitting a foreign related party beyond arm's length. Deduct only French-related provisions and amortisation, and exclude foreign-source income not taxed in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C / Résultat fiscal (taxable income or deficit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after statutory adjustments. Deficit shown with negative sign for carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident with a French PE must compute French-source taxable income as if the PE were an independent enterprise operating in France. Foreign losses cannot be used against French income except through treaty-compliant PE attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D / Déficits reportés (carryforward and carryback utilisation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of prior-year taxable losses against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: French PE losses may be carried forward under domestic rules, subject to the annual cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable surplus where applicable. Treaty PE losses previously deducted in the residence state cannot be reused in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E / Calcul de l'impôt (IS computation and credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate income tax at heading rate or reduced SME rate, plus the 3.3% social contribution where applicable, less tax credits and pre-payments, yielding net corporate income tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax credits such as the CIR and CII are reported proportionately where research is performed in France. The PE cannot claim foreign tax credits on the French return except where France grants a credit under treaty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing generates a 10% increase of assessed tax, rising to 20% after formal notice and 40% if not corrected within 30 days. Monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% of unpaid tax accrues. A failure to file can trigger taxation d'office, automatic assessments and exclusion from tax clearance certificates required for public procurement contracts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on gross dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders, reduced to 0% where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies (10% or greater shareholding, two-year holding attachment, substance and non-abuse conditions) and further reduced to 5% or 15% under many French income tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must submit a tax residence certificate (certificat de résidence) issued by the residence-country tax authority, together with a beneficial-ownership declaration and, where applicable, the specific treaty relief form required by the French payer. This documentation must be supplied to the French distributing company before the dividend payment so that the reduced treaty rate can be applied at source. If tax is withheld in excess, the recipient must file a reclaim with the DGFiP within the statutory limitation period, supported by the TRC and documentation proving ownership and economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-residents is generally free of French withholding tax, though treaty-protected rates may be 0%-10%. Royalties and similar intellectual-property payments are subject to a domestic withholding tax of 33.33%, often reduced to 0% or 10% under French treaties; payments routed to non-cooperative jurisdictions face severe anti-abuse penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A French Local File and Master File are mandatory where the French entity or the consolidated group exceeds total balance-sheet assets or gross turnover of EUR 400 million. A Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for ultimate parent groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. The franchised heavy electrical equipment manufacturer must maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation in French or English if within the scope.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) - méthode du prix comparable sur le marché libre
Resale Price Method - méthode du prix de revente
Cost Plus Method - méthode du coût majoré
Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) - méthode de la marge nette transactionnelle
Profit Split Method - méthode de répartition des bénéfices
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations, but anti-abuse rules, the abuse-of-right doctrine, CFC rules and beneficial-ownership clauses in treaties are vigorously applied. A French SAS must maintain actual management, engineering, inventory and decision-making functions in France; a hollow shell or letterbox entity using the French treaty network for conduit structures will be disregarded and reassessed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion (fraude fiscale) and deliberate false declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful understatement of taxable income, fabricated expenses, concealment of French fixed-base activity, use of artificial subcontracting invoices, or knowing participation in a mispriced transfer-pricing scheme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties of 40% to 80% on the additional tax, monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%, and automatic tax reassessment. Criminal conviction can result in imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to EUR 75,000, increased to EUR 750,000 when the proceeds of the fraud are laundered. The company may additionally lose government contracts and be excluded from tax settlement procedures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve false returns are exposed to criminal prosecution as co-perpetrators. The corporate veil may be pierced via the action en comblement de passif where fraudulent management caused the company to be unable to pay taxes; civil restitution, travel restrictions, judicial supervision and a ban on managing any French business for up to 15 years may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of rights and artificial shell company arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or maintaining a French SAS without autonomous commercial or operational substance, using the SAS solely to claim treaty withholding relief, export incentives, tax credits, or to channel high-voltage transformer profits to connected foreign parties while minimising French taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the doctrine d'abus de droit under Article L64 of the Livre des procédures fiscales, yielding 80% penalty on additional tax plus interest. The DGFiP may recharacterise transactions, disregard the shell entity and reassess the beneficial owner. Failure to maintain valid substance can also trigger penalisation under the anti-money-laundering regime for corporate registrants.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the abusive structure risk personal liability because the entity has no economic reality; courts may order personal payment of corporate tax and penalties, and the directors may be condemned for misuse of corporate assets (abus de biens sociaux). Judicial management bans and, in cross-border fraud cases, international travel bans apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation and intercompany charging failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the Local File/Master File within 30 days of a DGFiP request, failure to produce the CbC report where required, invoicing related parties at non-arm's-length margins, or providing incomplete functional and risk documentation for the French manufacturing operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty can reach 5% of the amount of the transfer-pricing adjustment, plus possible fixed penalties for failure to respond to a documentation request. The tax administration may increase French taxable income by the mispriced amount, apply interest and the standard 40% bad-faith penalty, and impose reporting fines for CbC breaches.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve non-arm's-length pricing may bear personal civil liability for the company's tax damage. Directors may also be jointly liable for the added tax where the billing structure is found to be a sham. In liquidation, the action en comblement de passif can reach directors who failed to put in place required transfer-pricing governance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Tracfin compliance red flags concerning payment rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the documentary-letter-of-credit or Swift-wire payment channel to launder fraud proceeds, conceal beneficial ownership through third-party payment intermediaries, process funds from embargoed jurisdictions, or deliberately fail to report suspicious movements to Tracfin where the entity holds a professional obligation to do so.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of EUR 375,000, increased in organised-crime circumstances. Administrative penalties may include withdrawal of licences, freezing of accounts and asset confiscation. The French Financial Intelligence Unit may also impose penalties for non-reporting by an accountable professional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly participating in laundering, or failing to prevent laundering when in control, may be prosecuted personally; personal fines and imprisonment can be imposed separately from corporate penalties. Directors' assets can be provisionally seized, they may receive a professional ban and travel bans are frequently imposed pending investigation.
